business_problem: Rapid growth across B2C and pharmacy channels was outpacing La Rosée Cosmétiques' legacy data platform, leaving sales, marketing, ecommerce, and product teams with siloed views of orders, inventory, and customer activity.
solution_summary: La Rosée Cosmétiques moved its fast-growing B2C and B2B data estate onto Snowflake so it could unify product, sales, and operational data before legacy systems created technical debt. Data from SAP, the online store, pharmacy sales, and operational processes now lands in Snowflake, which holds over 100 million rows across hundreds of tables and feeds Tableau visualizations for cross-functional teams. That shared foundation gives marketing, ecommerce, commercial, logistics, and product teams one view of orders, inventory, and customer behavior instead of each working from different datasets. The platform also lets the company reuse the same logic to launch ordering systems in new countries, resolve delayed shipments faster, and enrich insights with external datasets without re-architecting the stack. By standardizing on Snowflake as a modular backbone, La Rosée improved day-to-day decision-making while creating a scalable base for sustainability, product, and customer insight use cases.

Tableau consumes that governed data for visualization, while business teams use the resulting insight to track orders, inventory, logistics issues, and new-country rollout readiness.
